misconception_description: Student believes that the arithmetic operation - has higher precedence than the arithmetic operation /.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekBilanganPrima
kamus
  n, i : integer
  prima : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  if n < 2 then
    prima <- false
  else
    prima <- true
    for i <- 2 to n - 1 / 2 do
      if n mod i == 0 then
        prima <- false
      endif
    endfor
  endif
  output(prima)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student changed `range(2, num//2)` to `range(2, num - 4//2)`. Due to their misconception about operator precedence, they believe `num - 4//2` evaluates as `(num - 4)//2`, which they think provides a good upper bound for checking prime divisors (half of num-4). However, the expression actually evaluates as `num - (4//2)` = `num - 2` because division has higher precedence than subtraction. This means the loop will check many more divisors than intended, checking almost all numbers up to num-2 instead of roughly half of num. This changes the algorithm's behavior and will cause incorrect results for small numbers (e.g., for num=5, it checks range(2, 3) instead of range(2, 0.5) which the student expected).
